blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Mastery of basic formulas is essential for solving Work and Time problems efficiently.
Work done by individuals and multiple persons working together forms the foundation of individual work rates.
Work and efficiency share an inverse relationship with time taken to complete a task.
The Men–Days concept provides a standardized method to solve multi-worker variable-time problems.
Time & Work deals with how long a person or group of persons take to complete a work and their efficiency.

blocks.content: In SSC examination, questions are direct, formula-based and mostly one to two step problems.

items: If a person can complete a work in x days, then one day’s work = 1/x.

blocks.content:
Example 1:

A can complete a work in 10 days.

Work done by A in one day = 1/10

Example 2:

If a person does 1/8 work in one day, then total time = 8 days.

items: If A completes work in x days and B in y days, then combined work per day = (1/x + 1/y).

blocks.content:
Example 3:

A can do a work in 12 days and B in 18 days.

items: Efficiency is inversely proportional to time.
If efficiency ratio of A : B = x : y, then time ratio = y : x.

blocks.content:
Example 4:

A is twice as efficient as B. B takes 20 days.

Time taken by A = 10 days.

Example 5:

A can do a work in 10 days. He works for 4 days.



Work done = 4 × 1/10 = 2/5

Remaining work = 3/5.

Example 6:

10 men can do a work in 6 days.

15 men will take = 4 days.

Example 7:

A can do a work in 15 days and B in 20 days.

Time together = 60/7 ≈ 8.57 days.



Example 8:

A alone can do a work in 25 days.

Work done in 5 days = 1/5.

items: Men–Days concept and efficiency-based questions are frequently asked in SSC level exams.
Always compute one day's work fraction when combining work of two or more individuals.
Partial work problems require careful tracking of remaining work after a worker leaves or joins.

blocks.content:
• Take total work as 1.

• Use fractions for accuracy.

• Efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

• SSC avoids lengthy time–work questions.

Q1. A can complete a work in 20 days. How much work will he do in 5 days?

A. 1/2 B. 1/4 C. 1/5 D. 1/10



Q2. A and B can do a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. How long will they take together?

A. 6 days B. 7.2 days C. 8 days D. 9 days



Q3. 12 men can do a work in 10 days. How many days will 15 men take?

A. 6 B. 7 C. 8 D. 9
